fatal_errors: The proposed titanium addition does not reconstruct the target intervention: optimizing SPS temperature for a 30% AlFeNiCoCr-bonded ZrB2 cermet, with 1500 °C as the optimum.
The cited evidence concerns Ti-containing CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys and does not demonstrate improved corrosion of borides in molten aluminum or formation of the proposed Ti-rich protective layer.
The material composition, titanium concentration, processing route, molten-aluminum temperature, and exposure duration are not defined sufficiently to make the hypothesis reproducible.
The proposed mechanism is speculative and omits the target mechanism of binder fluidity, pore filling, densification, and binder loss at excessive sintering temperature.
explanation: The response addresses molten-aluminum corrosion of boride components and offers a nominally controlled comparison against an undoped baseline, but it is neither an exact nor partial reconstruction of the target study. The target varies SPS temperature for ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermets and attributes the optimum at 1500 °C to maximum densification and effective binder-mediated grain bonding. The generated hypothesis instead introduces titanium and asserts an unverified protective interfacial phase. E1 provides only remote evidence about Ti effects in bulk high-entropy alloys, not boride cermets exposed to molten Al, so it cannot support the central corrosion mechanism. The experiment could test the alternative in principle, but undefined composition and exposure conditions weaken discrimination, and its falsification rule improperly requires both corrosion improvement and observation of a particular mechanism. The idea is novel relative to the target but presently unsupported.
